chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Faddal, from Ahmad ibn Umar, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding
the man who throws the pellet and the stone and kills (the game) — can he eat from it? He said: Do not eat.

key_terms.الْبُنْدُقِ: Clay pellet or ball used as a projectile, fired from a sling or similar device
key_terms.الْحَجَرِ: A thrown stone used as a hunting implement
key_terms.لَا تَأْكُلْ: Categorical prohibition: do not eat — indicating the animal is not lawfully slaughtered

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to eat game killed by a stone or clay pellet?
ai.summary: This hadith records a ruling by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) on the permissibility of eating game animals killed by impact weapons such as clay pellets (bundq) or thrown stones. The Imam categorically prohibits consumption of such prey. In classical Islamic jurisprudence, lawful hunting requires that the animal either be slaughtered with a sharp instrument or killed by a trained hunting animal (like a dog or falcon), with the name of God invoked. Death by blunt impact — whether from a stone or clay ball — does not meet these requirements, making the animal akin to one that died from a blow (mawqudhah), explicitly prohibited in the Quran (5:3).

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ahmad Bin Umar, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who threw the pellet, and the stone, so he killed (a hunted prey), so can he eat from it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said:’ He cannot eat’.
en.sarwar: 7. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Ahmad ibn ‘Umar from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “About the case of a man who hits a prey with a stone or clay-ball and kills it;
if he can use it for food, he (the Imam) said, ‘Do not eat it.’”
